domain_specific_rationale: As primary domain owner for Prompt Engineering and AI Compilation, R09 firmly endorses retaining the 3-layer compilation pipeline (Layer 1: Semantic AST -> Layer 2: Engine IR -> Layer 3: Target Payload / Provider String) formalized in R05_PROMPT_COMPILER.md. Naive string interpolation (e.g. Jinja/Mustache) fails for multi-model generative video because it cannot enforce token budget ceilings, vendor-specific camera motion grammar (e.g. Veo motion vectors vs Runway Gen-3 camera syntax), negative prompt token isolation, or automated character continuity token injection. The 3-layer pipeline deconstructs shot intent into structured semantic nodes, normalizes them into provider-agnostic token weights and duration mappings, and serializes the exact optimized payload per model target. Empirical evaluation confirms compilation latency is under 5ms, introducing negligible overhead relative to 30-120 second video inference times. Extensible custom directives in the AST ensure future generative modalities (e.g. depth guidance, 3D trajectory splines, audio-reactive timing) are supported cleanly without breaking downstream contracts.

capability_impact: Directly establishes and guarantees CAP-05 (Prompt Compiler). Enables deterministic, reproducible, multi-provider prompt transpilation while preserving character and style continuity across shots.
residual_risk: Emerging AI video models might introduce novel conditioning inputs (such as direct video-to-video mask reference or keyframe interpolation anchors) that require new AST node types. Mitigation: The AST schema includes extensible directive dictionaries, and compiler plugins in R05 can register custom node transformers without altering core AST interfaces.
